He is a great professor! I was initially unsure but quickly realized that I got lucky being in his class. He truly cares about teaching and wants you to really understand the material, which is more than most professors can say. He is lenient and very fair on exams because he teaches the material thoroughly. I can't recommend him enough!

His tests are similar to practice exams, and if you read the textbook/go to class, the homework is not hard either.

Professor Yavari's course completely shocked me. I haven't met many professors who genuinely seem to care about their students understanding the content the way he does. His exams are extremely similar to his practice exams, and going to his office hours helps a ton. He's also extremely willing to work with you on your grade as long as you care.

attendnace at lecture is mandatory but I couldn't focus on his lectures or follow him most of the times he talks about topics as if students should already know about it, so I used the textbook and online resources to teach myself a lot of the topics there are long weekly hw that usually don't add anything to test prep, but focus on the sample exam

review_highlights.comment: She's a passionate teacher and very understanding! You learn skills that are truly relevant, there are weekly "responses" that are creating your own version of media (Instagram carousel, Canva flyer, etc.) and applying that to readings. At the end there's a final project with a non-profit to apply your skills that is super valuable professionally.

Dr. Allegra is easily the best professor I have ever had at Tech. She is so incredibly kind and her teaching is both interesting and engaging, as are the projects she assigns. She is an awesome professor overall and I can't recommend her enough!
Dr. Allegra Smith is a nice person and she is helpful, but I did not enjoy how much participation was required. I felt like being an introvert was a disadvantage in her course.
Dr. Allegra cares about her students and is extremely passionate about what she teaches! She cares about her students and helps you out if you ask for it.

One thing I love about Prof. Allegra is that she assigns work that she knows will prepare us for our future careers. One day we had a mock interview class, for example. She prioritizes quality of learning over everything, is understanding about grades, and does a good job of building relationships of mutual respect and understanding with students.

analysis.name: Ashok Goel
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I have very mixed feelings. I really like this professor, but CS7637 is the worst class I have taken yet at Georgia Tech. I learned more reading about the topics on Wikipedia than I did in lecture. This professor loves busy work too, so expect a bunch of pointless writing assignments. He just isn't a computer scientist, he's a cog psych guy.

I liked the professor and found his lectures fun, but the course itself felt disorganized and heavily overloaded with assignments. Many took a lot of time without reinforcing the material, so the workload felt inefficient. Overall, I found the experience frustrating and not very useful. I had high hopes, but the course didn't deliver.

A few problems I had with the class:
-Lectures are mandatory and long, and he always waits for 5 questions/comments from the class
-Assignments are writing heavy
-Class is more cog-sci focused than CS focused (one programming assignment was like 300 lines of if statements)
-part of your participation points are based off talking to AI TAs

Overbearing and uninspiring. Class is bloated with busy work and he throws a fit if you don't ask a question within 5 seconds of him asking if there are any questions. By taking this class, he will run cognitive science experiments on you as a student, which is something I definitely did not want to be a part of.

Course is well-structured and the professor supports his students. TA team is slightly inconsistent and aggressive in their approach to students (Head TA accused half the class of cheating in peer reviews). His accent makes it difficult to understand what he's saying at 1.4x speed. Overall, I liked the slow introduction to AI agents in this class.

review_highlights.comment: i took her for both foundations and corporate strategy. it definitely takes work to get an A, and you actually have to do all of the readings. however, it is very rewarding in the end because the class discussions are really fun. go to office hours if you want to do better on exams. also please actually contribute to the group project.
She is such a difficult teacher, the tests were nothing like the practice exams. She is scary.

Very harsh grader even if you put so much effort in. I had to take her for both foundations and corporate strategy, and it was awful. Lectures are very boring and long, be prepared to speak in every class for a good participation grade. Group essay at the end was a terrible idea and no matter how much you change, she doesn't give a good grade.

The case studies were actually very interesting, I enjoyed reading them. You have to participate a lot, and even if you do participate, you also have to go above and beyond for the group project. I had a very high grade until the group project, which was a very tedious and uninteresting process to do- lots of deliverables, and very strict grading.

One of my favorite professors I have ever had. Just know that it is not a walk in the park, it requires an honest effort to understand the material and to contribute to discussions. You get a ton of value out of the class if you genuinely participate. Show up to class prepared, her office hours are very helpful. Great professor

Attendance isn't mandatory, but I would strongly recommend going as he sometimes tests material not in the slides. Very caring guy too.

We just finished drawing the brachial plexus and although challenging it was fun to draw along with him on the whiteboard. I can't wait for Human Pathology

I was really struggling with anatomy and school/life  in general. He was the only professor that took the time with me outside of class to help me. I will forever be grateful for this man. I wish more professors on campus cared half as much as Dr. Decker did.

WE LOVE DR. DECKER! Genuinely the best prof I've had at GT. Lectures are engaging, go to them! Even if you can pass the class without attending, the things he says in person will stick with you for the rest of your medical career. Exams are a bit tough, make sure you deeply understand the content and are not just memorizing. Flashcards are a must!

Why is this called an intro class. Homeworks take min 6 hrs a week, TAs cant help much, it's too hard. Test reviews are so useless from TAs. If you get a C on 1 exam, no chance of an A.

Extremely hard class, DO NOT TAKE AT ANY COST, don't believe these fake reviews, this class genuinely felt like hell. Homeworks were extremely hard and took almost 20 hours per HW. Exams were similar to HW questions but 5 times harder. Extremely hard class and professor.

review_highlights.comment: I have attended 4 funerals this year and didn't shed a tear at any. I bawled after his final exam and midterms. No preparation provided except for literally nothing. This class was the definition of doom and despair and everything unfair. Matthieu Ratoslav will take your soul - do not take unless you want to cross the River Styx.

I don't think he deserves all the hate that these reviews have been giving him. The class was fair and the exams were very similar to the homework. He is a nice person and mostly accommodating. He is very slow, but he also doesn't normally teach, and his section was only added to accommodate the influx of freshmen. This is not a deadly class.

Professor Bloch is an extremely caring professor, who is always willing to distribute knowledge on any subject he has on hand. Signal processing, machine learning, life lessons, he has and will teach about anything. Being in this VIP course has taught me so much, even when I started from no knowledge at all.

Lied to our faces about exam questions multiple times. Emphasized proof-based math questions instead of engineering/ system design ones, where the slightest error could cost you half credit. Only covered half of the material listed in the syllabus; we have to catch up now. His reviews for the graduate-level classes have the exact same complaints.

We got to early October's material in December. He regularly makes promises he doesn't keep.

He has described his own grading scheme as brutal. Every (lengthy) question is 2 points. If you write down anything you get 1 point. If you get the entire problem correct with no small errors at all, you get 2 points. 85% of the course grade was exams.

review_highlights.comment: Brito's teaching pace is great, and he keeps class very interesting: extremely funny. Sometimes doesn't follow the textbook or slides, but normally his ideas are better and simpler than those presented. Struggled to fall asleep in linear algebra, that's a feat.

I loved this class and Professor Brito. One complaint however is with the TAs. This is the first class where TAs are less approachable than the Professor and this might be due to how the class is structured. Some TAs were really nice and helpful but others TAs (namely one) on Piazza who would demean students constantly with their replies.

Brito is a great professor who clearly has a passion for the material and can keep students engaged. HW seemed like a lot for me but it really helped me learn the material. There is adequate study material for each exam and Brito tries to keep the class as engaging as possible.

Being an easy professor who gives high grades despite failing exams does not translate to being a good professor. He never released homework answers or exam answers or even feedback, just whether it was correct or not. This made doing homework worthless. For the final, he explicitly said specific topics were not on the exam--they were on the exam.

His tests are easier than the other sections, which is big in 1553. His lectures are pretty funny and entertaining, and he's a really nice guy. At first I thought he was going to be really disorganized, but he really knows his stuff and he's pretty good at teaching if you pay attention.

review_highlights.comment: Mythical pull of a professor. Great professor. Lectures are engaging and clear. He clearly cares about his students. Goes question by question when explaining what is going to be on the test. You will not regret taking his class.

He's the best!! He clearly cares about his students and tries his best to make accounting fun. You don't really need to do the recommended textbook problems and he has videos on the concepts if you miss something in class.

Had this prof for MGT 4026, MGT 4029, and MGT 4043. His classes are straightforward with outlines and lectures videos you can refer back to. I wouldn't really recommend stacking his classes because he puts his exam dates on the same day for all of them.

BEST PROFESSOR AT SCHELLER! If you're considering taking Accounting 2101 with anyone other than Professor Blunck, DON'T. I can't stress enough how amazing he is. He set up his class in a manner that makes it easy for all his students to succeed. Accounting is a difficult subject, but Blunck made it much more digestible.

He had some times where he was rather derogatory and kind of feed you to the wolves mindset, but it did pressure me to try hard and learn so it worked. The first labs were hell tho and took forever.

Took 3011 with Brothers, this class is a lot of work but the junior design project made me feel super prepared for senior design and he is a great professor - very reasonable and likeable, and teaches the course well
